claims.quote: The basis of his claim is the fact that he is a man.
claims.description: Every citizen receives an equal share of the nation's goods based on nothing more than being human.

claims.quote: We require of each that he shall make the same effort; that is, we demand of him the best service it is in his power to give.
claims.description: Every worker is required to give the same maximum effort, with pay equal regardless of how much each produces.

claims.quote: The fact that the nation is the sole capitalist and land-owner of course restricts the individual's possessions to his annual credit
claims.description: The state owns all capital and land, and individuals hold only an annual credit plus personal belongings.

claims.quote: We require, indeed, by law that every man shall serve the nation for a fixed period, instead of leaving him his choice
claims.description: Every man is legally required to serve the nation in industry for a fixed period.

claims.quote: These halls are connected by telephone with all the houses of the city whose people care to pay the small fee
claims.description: Subscribers can connect by telephone from home to live concert halls and choose among simultaneous performances.

claims.quote: All our bedchambers have a telephone attachment at the head of the bed by which any person who may be sleepless can command music at pleasure
claims.description: Every bedroom has a telephone link that lets a sleepless person request music at any hour.

claims.quote: The orders, as they are taken by the different departments in the store, are sent by transmitters to him.
claims.description: Customers' orders are sent through pneumatic transmitters from store departments to a central warehouse dispatcher.
All goods belong to the nation, so store clerks take orders rather than selling.

claims.quote: His credit, like an annuity in your day, ceases on his death
claims.description: A citizen's annual credit ends at death, with only a fixed sum allowed for funeral expenses.
